title: Multi-Country Bundibugyo Ebola Outbreak Response (3-9 August 2026) - Situation Report #13
snippet:
4,449 confirmed Ebola cases and 2,061 deaths in the DRC as of 10 August 2026, making this the largest and fastest-growing Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak ever recorded in the country.
 Over 16.5 million health screenings supported at 225 points of entry and points of control across affected and at-risk countries.
 During the reporting period, IOM supported 2.57 million health screenings in the DRC alone [...] According to the World Health Organization, as of 10 August, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) reported 4,449 confirmed cases of Ebola disease caused by the Bundibugyo virus (BVD), including 2,061 deaths. [...] More than 13.1 million individuals reached through risk communication and community engagement activities.
 Trained 575 health workers in Rwanda on Ebola detection, infection prevention and control, surveillance, and response measures.
 Continued to strengthen surveillance and preparedness capacities along critical mobility corridors, including riverine routes into Kinshasa and border areas near South Sudan and the Central African Republic.

title: IOM Multi-Country Ebola Bundibugyo Outbreak Response Update - sitrep #12
snippet:
The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has reported 3,532 confirmed Ebola Bundibugyo cases and 1,556 deaths, making this the largest and fastest-growing BVD outbreak recorded in the country.
 IOM has supported over 12.2 million health screenings at 223 points of entry and points of control across affected and at-risk countries.
 More than 10.7 million people have been reached through risk communication and community engagement activities. [...] According to the World Health Organization, as of 29 July, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) reported 3,532 confirmed cases of Ebola disease caused by the Bundibugyo virus (BVD), including 1,556 deaths. [...] The spread of the outbreak into Tshopo and Haut-Uélé introduce new risks within these provinces, across the country and for the wider region. In Tshopo, patient movement in search of health care is contributing to further transmission, while the rising number of cases in Haut-Uélé requires enhanced disease surveillance and cross-border coordination to prevent disease transmission into neighbouring South Sudan and the Central African Republic (CAR).

title: Tracking the 2026 Ebola outbreak in maps and figures: Locations, severity, how contagious it is and more
snippet:
By Jane Weaver, Jiachuan Wu and Javier Zarracina

The ongoing Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo has alarmed global public health experts for the ferocity of the spread in the remote and heavily populated region. Since the World Health Organization declared a public health emergency in mid-May, there have been hundreds of confirmed cases and dozens of deaths from the Bundibugyo species of the virus. [...] The Bundibugyo virus was discovered in western Uganda less than 20 years ago. This is just the third time Bundibugyo has been the cause of an identified outbreak. Experts believe African fruit bats may be the source of the virus.

Jane Weaver

Jane Weaver is managing editor of the health and medical unit at NBC News.

Jiachuan Wu

Jiachuan Wu is a senior interactive journalist for NBC News Digital.

Javier Zarracina [...] There’s no vaccine or treatment for the Bundibugyo virus, although there are two potential vaccine candidates, according to the WHO. Neither is ready for testing on humans.

There are four species of the Ebola virus that are known to cause disease in humans, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

title: Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus
snippet:
As of 30 July 2026, a total of 3605 confirmed cases, including 1587 deaths (CFR 44%), have been reported in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. To date, 651 patients have recovered.

Cases have been reported from 49 health zones (HZ) across five provinces: Ituri (28/36 HZ), North Kivu (11/34 HZ), South Kivu (1/34 HZ), Haut- Uélé (5/13 HZ) and Tshopo (4/23 HZ). An additional HZ, Wanie-Rukula in Tshopo, is awaiting data harmonisation at the health province level. [...] Since 17 July 2026 when the last Disease Outbreak News was published, an additional 1481 confirmed cases, including 759 confirmed deaths, have been reported in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The increase is in part due to expansion of surveillance activities, enhanced laboratory testing, and diagnostic capacity. However, most of the increase reflects the expansion of the outbreak. [...] This outbreak is now the largest recorded Ebola disease outbreak in the country, surpassing the previous largest outbreak, which occurred from 2018 to 2020, and resulted in 3317 confirmed cases.
